summary.headline: Carysil Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 27% to INR56 crores with margin at 21.2%; management now tracks the upper band of the 18-20% FY27 guidance.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 16.5% YoY to INR264.8 crores, with EBITDA up 27% to INR56 crores and margin expanding 175 bps to 21.2%. PAT grew 37.7% YoY to INR31.4 crores (PAT margin 11.9%), and EPS was INR11.05 versus INR8.03. Management attributed the margin gain to operating leverage, product mix, US discount rollback and efficiency, and said it maintains 15% revenue growth guidance. Logistics-related container delays pushed some export dispatches into Q2, and the UK business was softer.

financial_highlights.change: +37.7% YoY (vs INR22.8 crores); PAT margin 11.9% (+183 bps)

segments.name: Quartz sinks
segments.commentary: Volume 2.01 lakh units, +6% YoY (from 1.89 lakh); about 51% of revenue. Capacity utilisation 88% on average in Q1, around 90% in June.

segments.name: Stainless steel sinks
segments.commentary: Volume 49.4 thousand units, +16% YoY; about 12% of revenue. Capacity raised by 70,000 to 250,000 units mid-quarter, utilisation 94% on weighted-average basis.

segments.name: Kitchen appliances
segments.commentary: Volume 9.8 thousand units, +12% YoY; about 11.8% of revenue. 53% of appliances sold were made in-house.

segments.name: Faucets
segments.commentary: Volume 12.5 thousand units, +43% YoY; 67% made in-house. Over 95% of faucet revenue is from India; export faucets not yet started.

segments.name: Surfaces / United Granite
segments.commentary: Surfaces about 25% of revenue per management. United Granite revenue grew over 20%, with gross margin said to have risen from 35% to 50% after higher-end stone inventory build.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of 15% for FY27 maintained (management describes it as a value guidance and a 5-year target of adding INR1,000 crores).
EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20% maintained; management says it is tracking towards the upper band.
Domestic momentum supported by a funded 90-day festive plan (September-November) and an 8-city celebrity roadshow.
Quartz sink expansion of 250,000 units on track for completion by end FY27 (March 2027).
Further 150,000 stainless steel sink capacity and 250,000 granite sink capacity targeted by March 2027.

FY27 capex of approximately INR80-90 crores: granite sinks INR40-50 crores, stainless steel about INR20 crores, faucets and appliances about INR20 crores. Management sees a minimum of INR50-60 crores of capex annually thereafter.
Carysil Blue D2C: first 10 stores in India targeted by end of calendar 2026 or March 2027. Surfaces fabrication unit in India targeted by March 2027.
Expected e-commerce sales in India to grow 3x this year; 180 stores over next two years, with 34 committed in Q2.
capex_capacity: Quartz sinks: 250,000-unit expansion on track for end FY27; management said infrastructure is built for half a million sinks.
Stainless steel: capacity added 70,000 units in Q1 (total 250,000), with 150,000 more by March 2027; new factory construction started on adjacent land.
Factory running close to 7 days a week per management, with utilisation near 90% and focus on productivity.
Surfaces (India) fabrication unit targeted for March 2027, with CNC automated process to be the first in India.
demand_pricing: Export order book described as the highest ever; new SKUs added with Lowe's, Home Depot and Amazon; Home Depot US and Canada partnership extended; Hafele Australia/NZ collaboration; first Amazon USA orders.
Logistics disruption delayed container dispatches at quarter-end, pushing some volume into Q2; management said material supply was not a constraint.
US discount rollback: about 90% completed, booked in the last month of Q1 (June). Lowe's display-sharing cost of USD3-4 million (50% share) expected to reverse, supporting margins.
India B2B is about 20% of India revenue (INR176 crores last FY); new builder breakthroughs include DLF and M3M.
Management cited pricing of INR12% average realisation growth in India domestic sales; stated average price held flat in FY27 guidance.
UK business softer in Q1 per management; new customers such as Bodel, Barwick and JJO added; project/builder segment being entered.
Faucet RO water system: first consignment sold out, about 60-day backlog.

qa_highlights.question: Why was quartz growth single digit and why were international subsidiaries and UK growth weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed logistics disruption and container delays that stopped dispatches at quarter-end despite strong order booking; UK is in a tight phase but new customers should drive recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Any price hikes taken across categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the ASP increase to operating leverage, US discount rollback, and a premium product mix in stainless steel and granite, rather than explicit price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 94% SS utilisation inclusive of the 70,000 units added in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity came mid-quarter, so utilisation is on a weighted-average days-available basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why was quartz capacity expansion structured as 250,000 units instead of 100,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand from export deals and India momentum required the larger expansion; it considers 20-25% spare capacity necessary at around 90% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% guidance a volume or value number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value guidance at 15%, and also stated 15% volume growth for the year, with average prices held; the answer was inconsistent and was not fully reconciled on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment revenue and domestic vs export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Quartz sink 51%, steel sink 12%, kitchen appliances 11.8%, surfaces 25%. Domestic INR56 crores and exports INR111 crores in Q1. Segment margins to be provided separately by IR or CFO.

risks_watch: Capacity constraints: factory at near-full utilisation, so volume growth depends on the timing of the March 2027 capacity additions.
Logistics and container delays shifting revenue from Q1 into Q2; check for catch-up in Q2 export dispatch.
UK market softness and dependence on new builder/project channels yet to show results.
Volume guidance ambiguity: the 15% volume figure was stated but conflicted with the Q1 volume growth of about 5-6% for quartz and steel combined; clarify the basis.
Sustaining the 27% EBITDA growth and upper-band margin as the US discount rollback and mix benefits normalise.
Faucet exports not yet started; capability and technology upgrades still in progress.

However, based on quarter 1 performance and trends we are seeing, we currently see ourselves tracking towards the upper band of that guidance.
So we are right now heavily booked. We probably have the strongest order booking position as of as of now.
The U.K. market expects to remain modest, we remain cautiously optimistic and see strong opportunities to gain market share through distribution channels.
Yes. 15% on the value and 15% on the volume across the categories. So we have maintained the same price levels as of now.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year trajectory and order book: management maintained the 15% revenue guidance and said it is tracking to the upper band of the 18-20% EBITDA margin guidance. It was cautious on UK demand ("modest") and logistics, and evasive on the 15% growth basis, with the volume-versus-value answers inconsistent and not reconciled on the call.

adds.what: 150,000-unit stainless steel sink capacity addition (after 70,000 added in Q1)
Surfaces fabrication unit in India (CNC automated)

growth.why: Management maintains 15% FY27 revenue growth (described as value guidance) and tracks the upper band of 18-20% EBITDA margin; backing is partial with quartz, stainless and granite capacity adds due by March 2027 (3 quarters), a highest-ever export order book, and FY27 capex of INR80-90 crore, though no specific revenue bridge was quantified.
